title: Drift Wood #17 · the photo
logline: The yearbook photo for the superlative. Wood has thoughts about composition.

panels.composition: The school hallway. A YEARBOOK PHOTOGRAPHER with a camera. WOOD posed against lockers, directing.

balloons.text: Lower. From below. Eisenstein. The subject should loom.

image.prompt: a teenage boy in an overcoat posed against school lockers directing a yearbook photographer to shoot from a lower angle

balloons.text: It's a yearbook. Everyone looms the same amount.

image.prompt: close-up of a patient student photographer with a camera

panels.composition: Wood, adjusting the overcoat collar, the trophy case behind him full of other people's trophies.

balloons.text: Then let the trophies loom. I'll provide contrast.

image.prompt: a teenage boy adjusting his overcoat collar in front of a trophy case full of trophies, school hallway

panels.composition: The photo, as it will run: Wood, dead center, slightly from below after all, looking like he already regrets it. Caption typeset under it.

characters.pose: in the photo, from slightly below

panels.caption: MOST LIKELY TO WIN A PULITZER — Arthur Finch

image.prompt: a yearbook photograph of a gaunt teenage boy in an overcoat shot from slightly below against lockers, looking like he already regrets the pose, typeset caption beneath
image.notes: The caption uses the author's real name — the yearbook's, not the strip's. It's a fact in the world of the strip, not a panel with the author in it: the photo is of Wood.

notes: The photo names Arthur Finch because the yearbook does. The strip lets it stand.
